nodes.title: Hecke's continuation for $d\equiv5\pmod8$ and the functional equation from Gauss's point count

nodes.summary: 1. Assume Tian–Yuan–Zhang's Theorem 3.5(2) in reading A, the Gross–Zagier statement, Gauss's point count, and, for every squarefree $d\equiv5\pmod8$, that the Hecke coefficients are multiplicative and satisfy the Hecke relation at the split primes. Then the class-number hypothesis in positive-rank form CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk holds. 2. Reading A, the Gross–Zagier statement and Gauss's point count imply CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk.
nodes.title: CR₃^TYZ_Cl,Rk from reading A, Gross–Zagier and Gauss's point count

nodes.summary: *Hecke's continuation for $d\equiv5\pmod8$* is the following assertion: for every squarefree natural number $d\equiv5\pmod8$, $L(C_d,s)$ has an entire continuation. It is the case of Hecke's continuation used by row 5b.
nodes.title: The continuation of $L(C_d,s)$ from Deuring's identity

nodes.summary: Deuring's identity says that the L-series of $C_d$ has the same coefficients as the Hecke L-series of $\psi_d$: $c_d(n)=\lambda_d(n)$ for every $n\ge1$, where $c_d(n)$ are the coefficients of the standard Euler product of $C_d$, which are those of $L(C_d,s)$ for odd squarefree $d$. Both sides are Euler products with quadratic local factors, so for odd squarefree $d$ it suffices to compare them at the primes.
nodes.title: Deuring's identity for $C_d$

nodes.summary: Hecke's continuation is stated for every $d\ne0$, while the computation of $L(C_d,s)$ covers odd squarefree $d$. This subsection removes both restrictions.
nodes.title: The L-series of $C_d$ for every $d\ne0$

nodes.summary: The functional equation of a periodic twist needs the finite Fourier transform $\hat c$ of the coefficient function $c$ to be supported on $(1+i)\mathbb Z[i]$ and to equal a constant multiple of $c$ there. For the finite part $\omega_d$ of the Hecke character, on $(\mathbb Z/4d)^2$, this subsection proves it with the constant $4d(1+i)\left(\frac2d\right)$ for every odd squarefree $d\equiv1\pmod4$.
nodes.title: The Fourier identity for the Hecke character

nodes.summary: 1. Hecke's continuation for $d\equiv5\pmod8$ and the functional equation on the critical strip both hold. 2. The functional equation on the critical strip holds: for every squarefree natural number $d\equiv5\pmod8$, every entire continuation $F$ of $L(C_d,s)$ and every complex $s$ with $0<\operatorname{Re}s<2$, $\Lambda_{32d^2}(2-s)=-\Lambda_{32d^2}(s)$.
nodes.title: The functional equation holds

nodes.summary: Let $\Lambda_N$ be the completed function of the functional equation: $\Lambda_N(s)=N^{s/2}(2\pi)^{-s}\Gamma(s)F(s)$ for a given $F$.
nodes.title: The functional equation from Deuring's identity and the Fourier identity

nodes.summary: For a prime $p\equiv1\pmod4$, the number of solutions of $y^2=x^3-x$ over $\mathbb F_p$ is $p+2A$, where $p=A^2+B^2$ and $-(A+Bi)$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $2+2i$. The proof here goes through a quartic Jacobi sum. Since $\mathbb Z[i]$ contains a primitive fourth root of unity, there is a character $\chi$ of $\mathbb F_p$ of order $4$ with values in $\mathbb Z[i]$; its square is the quadratic character. nodes.summary: This subsection is about the Gaussian integers, with one exception: the vanishing of $\lambda_d(p)$ at the primes $p\mid2d$ is read off from Deuring's identity at those primes. nodes.title: The Hecke character $\psi_d$ and its coefficients

nodes.summary: 1. Gauss's point count implies Hecke's continuation: for every natural number $d\ne0$, $L(C_d,s)$ has an entire continuation. 2. Gauss's point count implies Hecke's continuation and the functional equation on the critical strip. 3. Hecke's continuation holds.
nodes.title: Hecke's continuation holds

nodes.summary: Tian–Yuan–Zhang's Theorem 3.5(2) in reading A and Hecke's continuation for $d\equiv5\pmod8$ together imply Tian–Yuan–Zhang's row 5b.
nodes.title: Row 5b from reading A and Hecke's continuation for $d\equiv5\pmod8$

nodes.summary: This subsection carries out Hecke's method for the Gaussian integers, with no reference to elliptic curves.
